Configure file storage access for specific IP addresses or subnets

Last update: October 05 2026Open in Markdown

You can configure file storage access for:

  • all IP addresses of the private subnet where the storage is located;
  • specific IP addresses;
  • other private subnets.

To configure access to the file storage, you need to add rules or delete rules. For each rule, you can select a specific access level. Rules can be added:

  • when creating a file storage;
  • or for an existing file storage.

Access levels

Depending on the file storage protocol, you can assign an access level to the storage:

  • for CIFS SMBv3 — read and write (rw);
  • for NFSv4 — read-only (ro), read and write (rw).

Add rule

For your information

A new access rule list for file storages with the NFSv4 protocol is applied within 15 minutes after adding or deleting rules.

Rules are applied in the order they appear in the list — from top to bottom:

  • a rule for accessing the storage from any IP address of a private subnet (0.0.0.0/0);
  • access rules from private subnets (for example, 192.168.0.0/29);
  • access rules from specific IP addresses (for example, 192.168.0.10).
note

For example, if the rules 0.0.0.0/0, 192.168.0.0/29, 192.168.0.1 are added, access to the storage will be open from any IP address of the private subnet.


  • Control panel

  • OpenStack CLI

  1. In the control panel, in the top menu, click Products and select File Storage.

  2. Open the file storage page → Access rules tab.

  3. Click + Add rule.

  4. Enter an IP address or the CIDR of the private subnet.

  5. Select an access level.

  6. Optional: enter a comment for the rule.

  7. Click Save.

  8. Optional: to add an additional rule, click + Add rule.

  1. Open the OpenStack CLI.

  2. Create an access rule:

openstack share access create <share> ip <ip_address> --access-level ro

Specify:

  • <share> — name or ID of the file storage. You can view the list of file storages using the command openstack share list;
  • <ip_address> — IP address or subnet CIDR to grant access to the file storage;
  • optional: --access-level ro — access level to file storage with the NFSv4 protocol for read-only access. If you do not specify the parameter, the default value will be rw — read and write access.

Resize file storage

warning

Once you increase the size of the file storage, it cannot be decreased. After you increase the storage, the tariff will change: we will refund the unused days of the previous tariff and charge for the new one.

This instruction describes how to resize file storage created in the Control panel after June 13, 2023.

If you created a file storage via technical support before June 13, 2023, to increase the storage size, submit a ticket and specify the new storage size in it.

  • Control panel

  • OpenStack API

  1. Unmount the file storage from the server.

  2. In the Control panel, in the top menu, click Products and select File Storage.

  3. Open the file storage page → Settings tab.

  4. In the Size field, click Edit.

  5. Specify the size of the file storage.

  6. Check the price of the file storage. After you increase the storage, the tariff will change: we will refund the unused days of the previous tariff and charge for the new one.

  7. Click .

  8. Mount the file storage back to the server.

  1. Unmount the file storage from the server.

  2. Get a project-scoped IAM token (X-Auth-Token).

  3. In the request output, copy the X-Subject-Token value.

  4. Open the CLI.

  5. Resize the file storage:

    curl 'https://<pool>.cloud.api.selcloud.ru/share/v2/shares/<filestorage_uuid>/action' \
      -H 'X-Auth-Token: <x_auth_token>' \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/json;charset=utf-8' \
      --data-raw '{"os-extend":{"new_size":<filestorage_size>}}'

    Specify:

    • <pool> — pool where the file storage was created, for example, ru-9. You can find the list of pools where file storage is available in the File Storage section of the Product availability by location guide;
    • <filestorage_uuid> — file storage ID. You can find the ID in the Control panel: in the top menu, click Products and select File Storage → in the row of the required storage, click ;
    • <x_auth_token> — IAM token for the project that you copied in step 2;
    • <filestorage_size> — new file storage size in GB, for example, 150. Size limit — 50 TB.

  6. Mount the file storage back to the server.
